title: What Healing Should Be: How to Relieve Pain and Stop Suffering
author: Dr. Amit Sood
target_audience: Individuals suffering from chronic pain or emotional suffering
Patients seeking holistic approaches to well-being
Healthcare professionals interested in integrative or compassion-based medicine
General readers interested in mental wellness, resilience, and healing
core_themes: Healing as a multidimensional, holistic process
The inseparability of physical pain and emotional suffering
Empathy, compassion, and self-kindness as tools for relief
The limits of the biomedical model in addressing suffering
primary_purpose: To redefine the meaning of true healing by blending scientific evidence, clinical experience, and practical wisdom, and to empower readers with strategies to relieve both pain and suffering—encouraging a shift from a purely symptom-focused model to a compassionate, whole-person approach.

structure_format.narrative_style: Warm, compassionate, and authoritative with a blend of storytelling, research summaries, and practical exercises
structure_format.organization: Split into thematic chapters that address foundational concepts, scientific evidence, patient stories, and actionable strategies
features: Summaries of neuroscientific and psychological research
Suggested practice plans and reflection prompts

key_concepts_lessons: Pain and suffering, while related, are not the same—pain is a physical sensation, but suffering is how we experience and process it.
Modern medicine is reliable for treating physical injuries or disease but often falls short in alleviating deeper suffering.
Engaging mindfully with your pain and practicing compassion can significantly reduce suffering, even if pain itself persists.
Healing should encompass not just the body but also the mind, relationships, and sense of purpose.
Building daily habits—like gratitude, acceptance, and mindful awareness—lay a foundation for long-term well-being.
Self-kindness and seeking support from others are central to any healing journey.
notable_features: Combines neuroscience, psychology, and patient perspective
Practical, evidence-based strategies for both body and mind
Highlights the importance of meaning and community in healing
Written by a respected physician with expertise in resilience and stress management
cultural_historical_context: Published in the early 2020s amidst a rising interest in integrative medicine and mental health, the book responds to widespread frustration over conventional healthcare’s limits in managing chronic suffering, especially post-pandemic.
reception_impact: Praised for reconciling scientific rigor with humanity and compassion
Accessible to both patients and healthcare providers
Valued for actionable advice and real-world case examples
Contributes to ongoing conversations about redefining health and care in medicine
comparable_titles: The Body Keeps the Score by Bessel van der Kolk
When the Body Says No by Gabor Maté
Full Catastrophe Living by Jon Kabat-Zinn
